<STRUCT_0001>
We can use this lemma to show the following important result; we also
give a proof avoiding fpqc descent.
We will discuss this and related results in more detail in
<ACCENT_0001>tale Morphisms, Section <REF_0001>.
A universally injective <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism is an open immersion.

First proof<PROOFARGEND_0001>Let <MATH_0001> be an <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism which is universally injective.
Then <MATH_0002> is open
(Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0001>)
hence we can replace <MATH_0003> by <MATH_0004> and we may assume that <MATH_0005> is surjective.
Then <MATH_0006> is bijective and open hence a homeomorphism. Hence <MATH_0007> is
quasi-compact. Thus by
Lemma <REF_0002>
it suffices to show that <MATH_0008> is a monomorphism. As <MATH_0009> is <ACCENT_0002>tale
the morphism <MATH_0010> is an open immersion by
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0003>
(and
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0004>).
As <MATH_0011> is universally injective <MATH_0012> is also surjective, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0005>.
Hence <MATH_0013> is an isomorphism, i.e., <MATH_0014> is a monomorphism.

Second proof<PROOFARGEND_0001>Let <MATH_0001> be an <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism which is universally injective.
Then <MATH_0002> is open (Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0001>)
hence we can replace <MATH_0003> by <MATH_0004> and we may assume that <MATH_0005> is surjective.
Since the hypotheses remain satisfied after any base change, we conclude
that <MATH_0006> is a universal homeomorphism. Therefore <MATH_0007> is integral, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0002>.
It follows that <MATH_0008> is finite by
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0003>.
It follows that <MATH_0009> is finite locally free by
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0004>.
To finish the proof, it suffices that <MATH_0010> is finite locally
free of degree <MATH_0011> (a finite locally free morphism of degree <MATH_0012>
is an isomorphism).
There is decomposition of <MATH_0013> into open and closed subschemes
<MATH_0014> such that <MATH_0015> is finite locally free of
degree <MATH_0016>, see Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0005>.
If <MATH_0017> is not empty, we can pick a morphism <MATH_0018>
where <MATH_0019> is an algebraically closed field (just take the algebraic
closure of the residue field of some point of <MATH_0020>).
Then <MATH_0021> is a disjoint union of
copies of <MATH_0022>, by
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0006>
and the fact that <MATH_0023> is algebraically closed.
However, since <MATH_0024> is universally injective, there can only be
one copy and hence <MATH_0025> as desired.
